messages:
Priya: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — we keep seeing tail latency spikes in dashboard queries. I dug into traces and it looks like the mux is queuing slow projection requests and holding up the fast-path. Need an ownership split proposal so we can land the refactor without surprising ops.
Ankur: Can you paste the trace sample? is it single-request queuing or head-of-line blocking across tenants?
Priya: Sample: most tails are from a small set of projections that do heavy joins and timeout at ~550ms. When mux batches, those long projections block the per-route worker for other fast tiny panels. Traces attached: `trace/1805550000/mux-1201.json` (summary inline).
Maya: Sounds like we need two levers: 1) separate execution lanes for long/short queries, 2) bounded-priority enqueue so heavy projections can't steal worker cores. Both need API/interface decisions though — who owns classification?
Ben: Agreed. Option A: mux classifies by estimated cost (seq_len, model of cost) and routes heavy to projection-service queue. Option B: projection-service exposes a cheap preflight checksum that the mux calls to decide. Tradeoffs: A keeps routing logic central, B pushes cost estimation to the service but adds an extra roundtrip.
Sam: For latency + simplicity I'd prefer A. We already have batch size + seq_len heuristics in mux; adding a lightweight cost estimator there is minimal. But we must avoid stale heuristics — need telemetry to retrain thresholds.
Ankur: Operationally, Option A means mux becomes RBAC-aware for routing (need to preserve tenant auth contexts). Do we want mux to hold those tokens? That has compliance implications.
Jun: If mux holds tokens we increase attack surface. Instead, we can carry a provenance header: `X-Projection-Intent: heavy|light` — generated by mux without storing creds, and projection-service re-checks permission on receipt. That keeps auth checks centralized in projection-service.
Priya: That header pattern looks good. So ownership split: mux owns classification + tagging; projection-service owns final auth checks and execution lane enforcement. We should document the exact header contract and failure modes.
Maya: We also need an SLO change: fast-path panels must remain <100ms p95. Projections exceeding slow threshold should be route-limited and optionally rate-limited per-tenant.
Ben: Implementation checklist proposal: 1) Mux: add cost estimator + header emission (PR1). 2) Projection svc: accept header, revalidate token, implement lane queue (PR2). 3) Console: add telemetry dashboard for misclassified requests + threshold tuning (PR3). 4) Ops: rollout canary with `X-Projection-Intent: test` and sampled replay.
Ankur: One more: failure fallback. If projection-service rejects a heavy tag (auth or overload), mux should have a fallback: either degrade to cached snapshot or return 429 depending on route config. Make that configurable per-route.
Priya: Agreed. Also add a per-tenant circuit-breaker in projection-service.
Sam: I can own PR1 (mux changes) and the cost-estimator quick prototype. Target: small canary in staging by next week.
Jun: I'll take PR2 (projection lane design + auth recheck). I'll add an auth checklist for external review.
Maya: I'll sketch the telemetry dashboard and thresholds in Console. Will include a metric: `projection_intent_mismatch_rate` and `fastpath_p95_by_route`.
Ben: Ops: I will prepare rollout runbook + canary config; include `--emit-intent: dry-run` mode for 72h.
infra-bot: Deploy bot scheduled staging canary for mux PR1 on 1805552400 (ETA) :rocket:
Priya: Sweet. Let's capture the header contract and the per-route fallback options in the RFC follow-up doc. I'll create a short spec and link PRs here. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
thread_summary: Decision to split ownership: mux will classify requests and emit an `X-Projection-Intent` header; projection-service revalidates auth and enforces execution lanes. Action owners assigned for mux, projection svc, console telemetry, and ops rollout.
